record.paper_title: Some open problems and research directions in the mathematical study of fluid dynamics.
record.original_question: For the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with constant density, kinematic viscosity ν > 0, divergence-free velocity field u(x,t), pressure p(x,t), no external energy input, and the usual whole-space, periodic, or no-slip bounded-domain settings, what are the most general smooth initial velocities u(x,0) that guarantee the solution exists for every positive time and remains smooth?

evidence.quote: What are the most general conditions for smooth incompressible velocities u(x, 0)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations for a fluid of constant density and kinematic viscosity ν > 0:

  ∂_t u + (u · ∇)u − ν Δu + ∇p = 0,   ∇ · u = 0,

where u(x,t) ∈ ℝ³ is the velocity field and p(x,t) ∈ ℝ is the pressure, posed on one of the following standard spatial domains: the whole space ℝ³ (with appropriate decay at infinity), the three-dimensional torus 𝕋³ (periodic boundary conditions), or a bounded smooth domain Ω ⊂ ℝ³ with the no-slip boundary condition u|_{∂Ω} = 0. There is no external forcing.

A smooth initial velocity is a divergence-free vector field u₀ : domain → ℝ³ belonging to C^∞ (with appropriate decay or boundary compatibility).

Determine the most general class of such smooth divergence-free initial data u(x,0) = u₀(x) for which the corresponding solution (u,p) exists globally in time (for all t > 0) and remains smooth (i.e., u(·,t) ∈ C^∞ for every t > 0).

Equivalently, characterize sharp sufficient conditions on u₀ that guarantee global-in-time smoothness of the resulting Leray solution and rule out any finite-time singularity.
artifact.status_search_result: The global regularity of 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes from general smooth initial data is one of the Clay Millennium Prize Problems and remains open. Only partial results exist (small data, axisymmetric without swirl, various conditional/regularity criteria such as Ladyzhenskaya–Prodi–Serrin and Beale–Kato–Majda, and Koch–Tataru small-BMO⁻¹ data), but no general characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness — Clay Mathematics Institute
status_evidence.snippet: The Clay Mathematics Institute lists global existence and smoothness for 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes as an unsolved Millennium Problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of global smoothness of 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes from smooth initial data is open.
